evaluations.affirmative_summary: Manual 5.3 and Prilog 2 assign management, QA, department and project duties. QA can identify problems, seek solutions, verify action and report directly to empowered management. Ekonerg retains responsibility for delegated work.
evaluations.contrary_summary: The text gives organizational freedom and direct reporting, but independence from cost and schedule pressure when safety is at stake is less explicit. Do not treat worker safety-reporting clauses as a nuclear QA stop-work rule.
evaluations.judge_ruling: Substantially matched, 4/5. Written QA authority and interfaces are present; one important independence safeguard needs clearer wording.
evaluations.rationale: Appendix B I / NQA-1 Part I Requirement 1: Manual 5.3 and Prilog 2 sections 1.2-1.3 provide substantive controls, not just a standard reference. Retain 75 points. Verify QA escalation when safety conflicts with cost or schedule.

evaluations.affirmative_summary: Manual 4.3 defines technical services and nuclear QA scope. Sections 7.1-7.2, 8.1 and 9.3 require competence, resources, graded project quality plans and annual documented management review. Dodatak 1 adds nuclear requirements.
evaluations.contrary_summary: The program refers to NQA-1 without an edition in its reference list. Nuclear project scope, quality levels and lower-level procedure applicability must be made clear in the project plan; the general manual alone does not settle each contract's scope.
evaluations.judge_ruling: Substantially matched, 4/5. The program has a usable documented structure, with project-specific scope and baseline details still to resolve.
evaluations.rationale: Appendix B II / NQA-1 Part I Requirement 2: concrete planning, training and review duties support 75 points. A cover statement of alignment is only a lead, not proof of complete alignment.

evaluations.affirmative_summary: Manual 8.3 covers design inputs, outputs, review, independent verification and changes. The nuclear addendum requires pre-use software checks, verification of level-I results and control of changes by the original responsible organization.
evaluations.contrary_summary: The nuclear addendum and Prilog 5 use inconsistent RSP/ROS procedure references. The complete software verification procedure is not supplied. Confirm the controlling method and its required acceptance, configuration and verification records.
evaluations.judge_ruling: Substantially matched, 4/5. Design control is documented, but its software/procedure reference chain needs clarification.
evaluations.rationale: Appendix B III / NQA-1 Part I Requirement 3: Manual 8.3 and Dodatak 1 point 3 support design control beyond generic intent. Retain 75 points; do not infer a complete software QA program from a procedure title.

evaluations.affirmative_summary: Manual 8.4 requires procurement scope, technical requirements, tests, inspections, acceptance criteria, review and approval. It also requires QA responsibilities, supplier access, nonconformance reporting, qualification needs and delivered quality evidence. Prilog 2 assigns QA flow-down responsibility.
evaluations.contrary_summary: The supplied policy does not fully spell out all lower-tier flow-down and record retention/submittal obligations for each nuclear purchase. Check those requirements in the controlled procurement procedure and contract template.
evaluations.judge_ruling: Substantially matched, 4/5. The full manual supplies procurement content that was missing from the earlier extraction.
evaluations.rationale: Appendix B IV / NQA-1 Part I Requirement 4: Manual 8.4.1-8.4.2 explicitly defines purchase-document content and contractual inclusion. Raise 50 to 75 points. This is based on the content of the new controls, not ten new crumbs.

evaluations.affirmative_summary: Manual chapter 3 defines qualified procedures and special processes. Section 8.5.2 requires validation and supervision when special processes are used. Dodatak 1 point 9 adopts that clause for nuclear work. Prilog 5 identifies RVT, RPT, RMT and RUT procedures as follow-up leads.
evaluations.contrary_summary: The register does not show the procedures' personnel/equipment qualification rules, process parameters, acceptance standards or qualification-record controls. Scope remains vague for coatings, concrete, epoxy/cement mixtures, non-metal visual testing and carbon laminates; do not assume these activities are performed.
evaluations.judge_ruling: Partially matched, 3/5. Control is recognized and conditionally required; the technical qualification layer is not available for full assessment.
evaluations.rationale: Appendix B IX / NQA-1 Part I Requirement 9 paragraphs 200-400: raise 0 to 50 points. Credit the written validation/supervision duty, not the existence of NDT procedure names as if they were qualification proof.

evaluations.affirmative_summary: Manual 7.5 and 8.1 establish procedure levels, project work plans, needed equipment and staff, technical standards, verification stages and acceptance criteria. Existing reviewed procedures supply work sequence and responsibilities.
evaluations.contrary_summary: Prilog 5 is a procedure register, not the work instructions themselves. Some referenced nuclear and special-process instructions are absent, so their quantitative or qualitative acceptance criteria cannot be confirmed from their titles.
evaluations.judge_ruling: Substantially matched, 4/5. The written instruction system is present; detailed acceptance instructions are not complete in the supplied set.
evaluations.rationale: Appendix B V / NQA-1 Part I Requirement 5: Manual 7.5 and 8.1 plus the retained procedure evidence support 75 points. Keep referenced instructions as leads until their actual text is reviewed.

evaluations.affirmative_summary: Manual 1.2 and 7.5.3 describe preparation, review, approval, revision, controlled distribution and withdrawal of obsolete documents. The nuclear addendum addresses approval of changes and distribution responsibility.
evaluations.contrary_summary: The full manual contains inconsistent live cross-references: Dodatak 1 points to ROS-02 for program controls, while Prilog 5 lists ROS-03; its record-backup clause names RSP-03 while the register lists ROS-04 for backups. The test crosswalk also points to 8.1.4 rather than 9.1.4. Resolve these before relying on the reference chain.
evaluations.judge_ruling: Substantially matched, 4/5. Document-control rules are strong, but the new full source reveals cross-reference defects that rule out a full match.
evaluations.rationale: Appendix B VI / NQA-1 Part I Requirement 6: lower 100 to 75 points for observed document clarity/control defects, not because execution records are absent. Compare Prilog 5, Dodatak 1 points 11 and 17, and its comparison table. A later procedure revision alone is not proof of a defect in an older manual.

evaluations.affirmative_summary: Manual 8.4 requires supplier evaluation, purchase verification and a written verifier report. The nuclear addendum includes dedication using safety functions and critical characteristics. Its flow notes require pre-engagement and periodic audits of level-I suppliers, subject to the stated qualified-list exception.
evaluations.contrary_summary: The full supplier/dedication method and acceptance evidence are not supplied for each purchase route. Confirm how critical characteristics, verification methods and acceptance before use are controlled; do not treat a dedication commitment as a completed dedication.
evaluations.judge_ruling: Substantially matched, 4/5. Selection, verification and follow-up controls exist, with some detailed acceptance routes still referenced elsewhere.
evaluations.rationale: Appendix B VII / NQA-1 Part I Requirement 7: retain 75 points using Manual 8.4 and Dodatak 1. This checks Ekonerg's control of supplier work; other companies do not become separate audit targets.

evaluations.affirmative_summary: Manual 8.5.3 maintains work-order and document identity throughout engineering delivery. Sections 7.5.4 and 8.5.5 link records and preservation to the item/service. Dodatak 1 point 8 commits to a nuclear identity/status document with traceability methods and marking authority where needed.
evaluations.contrary_summary: The nuclear item-identification method is deferred to a project document not supplied here. Controls for marking transfer, limited-life items and maintaining identity in storage are not developed in this manual. Apply these hardware duties only where the contract involves such items.
evaluations.judge_ruling: Partially matched, 3/5. There is real service/document traceability and a nuclear control commitment, but the detailed item-control layer remains incomplete.
evaluations.rationale: Appendix B VIII / NQA-1 Part I Requirement 8 paragraphs 200-303: raise 0 to 50 points. The former no-evidence conclusion was an extraction failure. Manual 8.5.3, 8.5.5 and Dodatak 1 point 8 support this bounded assessment.

evaluations.affirmative_summary: Manual 9.1.4 requires independent verification, acceptance checks and planned witness/hold points. Sections 8.4.3 and 8.6 link verification reports, conformity and authorized release. Existing procedure evidence supports inspection responsibilities.
evaluations.contrary_summary: Confirm that inspection independence excludes both the performer and direct supervisor, and that any hold-point waiver is recorded before work continues. The supplied text does not fully establish those NQA-1 details for every inspection route.
evaluations.judge_ruling: Substantially matched, 4/5. Inspection and release controls are documented; independence and waiver details need clarification.
evaluations.rationale: Appendix B X / NQA-1 Part I Requirement 10 paragraphs 100, 300 and 600: retain 75 points. A future field audit should sample records, but their absence is not the sole reason for this documentation rating.

evaluations.affirmative_summary: Manual 9.1.4 requires customer test programs and procedures with requirements, acceptance criteria, test conditions, documented results and evaluation. Section 8.1 requires planned testing needs. The nuclear flow notes state software result/pre-use verification triggers.
evaluations.contrary_summary: The manual says Ekonerg does not test its own services/products and develops programs for customer testing. Detailed test prerequisites, instrument suitability, configuration and minimum record fields are not fully shown. ROS-02 is referenced but not supplied, and Prilog 5 lists ROS-03 as program-use control.
evaluations.judge_ruling: Partially matched, 3/5. A test-control policy exists; complete test and software-verification methods remain incomplete in the supplied set.
evaluations.rationale: Appendix B XI / NQA-1 Part I Requirement 11 paragraphs 100-300, 500-601: raise 0 to 50 points. Preserve the source's customer-testing qualification. Do not add blanket Part II requirements through this assessment.

evaluations.affirmative_summary: Manual 7.1.5 and retained procedures require calibration intervals, checks before infrequent use, records, status marking and exclusion of overdue equipment. Repeatedly inaccurate equipment is repaired or replaced.
evaluations.contrary_summary: The reviewed text does not fully establish evaluation of past results back to the last acceptable calibration after loss/damage or out-of-calibration findings, nor the complete use/application traceability chain. The commercial ruler/tape/level exception is allowed by NQA-1 when required accuracy is met; it is not itself a defect.
evaluations.judge_ruling: Partially matched, 3/5. Core calibration controls exist, but retrospective impact and use-traceability requirements need clearer support.
evaluations.rationale: Appendix B XII / NQA-1 Part I Requirement 12 paragraphs 303.1-303.2 and 304: retain 50 points with a corrected technical reason. Missing calibration certificates alone do not decide the documentation score.

evaluations.affirmative_summary: Manual 8.5.5 requires identification, handling, storage, cleaning, packaging, preservation and transport controls. It requires specific instructions, special-environment marking and periodic checks, suitable equipment and trained/experienced handlers. Dodatak 1 point 13 applies these controls to nuclear work.
evaluations.contrary_summary: The manual does not clearly require inspection/testing of special handling tools at specified intervals or before use. Confirm that requirement in the relevant project instruction, where special tools are used.
evaluations.judge_ruling: Substantially matched, 4/5. Most preservation duties are explicit; a specific special-tool assurance duty remains unclear.
evaluations.rationale: Appendix B XIII / NQA-1 Part I Requirement 13 paragraphs 100-600: raise 0 to 75 points. This is substantive coverage in Manual 8.5.5, not just the addendum's cross-reference.

evaluations.affirmative_summary: Manual 7.1.5 excludes overdue equipment. Sections 8.6 and 9.1.4 require acceptance/release endorsement. Dodatak 1 point 14 requires a specific nuclear status-marking document where needed, including methods, traceability and marking authority.
evaluations.contrary_summary: The specific status document is not supplied. The exact rules for applying/removing status marks, preventing bypass of tests and preventing unintended operation of affected equipment are not demonstrated by release approval alone.
evaluations.judge_ruling: Partially matched, 3/5. Release and calibration status controls exist, but the broader nuclear item/operating-status scheme is still a deferred detail.
evaluations.rationale: Appendix B XIV / NQA-1 Part I Requirement 14: raise 0 to 50 points using Manual 8.6, 9.1.4 and Dodatak 1 point 14. Operating-status checks are bounded to equipment affected by Ekonerg work.

evaluations.affirmative_summary: Manual 8.7 requires identification, marking, segregation or other misuse prevention, evaluation, authorized disposition and reinspection. It records customer agreement and approvals. Dodatak 1 point 15 adds nuclear nonconformance and Part 21 duties through PQ10.2-1.
evaluations.contrary_summary: The reviewed control set does not fully show technical justification and design-control treatment for repair/use-as-is, required as-built updates and the competence/access criteria for disposition evaluators. Part 21 customer notification is not by itself proof of all statutory reporting duties.
evaluations.judge_ruling: Partially matched, 3/5. Basic nonconformance control is substantive, but important nuclear disposition details remain insufficiently supported.
evaluations.rationale: Appendix B XV / NQA-1 Part I Requirement 15 paragraphs 403-405: retain 50 points on specific documentation gaps, not merely a lack of completed NCRs. Manual 8.7 and Dodatak 1 point 15 replace the earlier overly narrow evidence explanation.

evaluations.affirmative_summary: Manual 8.7, 9.2, 10.2 and Prilog 2 require prompt identification and action, cause analysis for significant or repeated problems, recurrence prevention, recorded results, management reports and verified completion/effectiveness. PQ10.2-2 revision 10 sections 2.2, 2.5, 2.7 and 3.1-3.8 assign the cause, approval, follow-up, reopening and reporting duties. These are written controls, not only standard references.
evaluations.contrary_summary: The real audit still needs samples showing timely closure and effective recurrence prevention. Separately, confirm the applicable Part 21 reporting path beyond customer notification in PQ10.2-1 section 3.11. Neither an unchecked work sample nor that separate reporting question is a missing Appendix B XVI corrective-action policy.
evaluations.judge_ruling: Fully matched for documentation, 5/5. The supplied written controls cover Appendix B XVI and NQA-1 Part I Requirement 16 paragraph 100. This is not a claim of verified field performance or full Part 21 compliance.
evaluations.rationale: Raise 75 to 100 points: the previous deduction was based on a separate Part 21 reporting check rather than a missing corrective-action duty. Linked manual crumbs APP_B_XVI-0004, 0007, 0008 and 0010 show significant/repeated cause review, prompt action, prevention of recurrence, records, verification and management reports; PQ10.2-2 revision 10 provides assigned implementation/follow-up duties. Keep Part 21 and completed-action sampling as explicit audit follow-up. Apply the document-scoring rubric of 2026-10-07 without changing the approved five-level weights.

evaluations.affirmative_summary: Manual 7.5.4 and retained record procedures cover identification, readable/retrievable records, retention and responsibility. Design, calibration, release and nonconformance records are specified. Dodatak 1 point 17 requires central archives, server storage and copies at a separate location.
evaluations.contrary_summary: The nuclear backup clause cites RSP-03, while Prilog 5 lists ROS-04 for server backup and RSP-03 for design documentation. Resolve the actual controlling storage/backup instruction and confirm the preservation method meets the applicable records requirements.
evaluations.judge_ruling: Substantially matched, 4/5. Record-control coverage is strong, but a concrete backup-control reference defect prevents a full match.
evaluations.rationale: Appendix B XVII / NQA-1 Part I Requirement 17: lower 100 to 75 points because the full manual exposes an unresolved preservation-control reference. This is not a downgrade simply for missing sample records; verify the correct instruction and its storage/retention controls.

evaluations.affirmative_summary: Manual 9.2 requires planned annual audits with defined criteria, scope and methods; trained independent auditors; reports and records; and verified corrective follow-up. Management review uses audit results. Nuclear supplier audits are addressed in the addendum and flow notes.
evaluations.contrary_summary: Confirm the detailed lead-auditor qualification and maintenance requirements and how deficient areas trigger follow-up or reaudit. A title in a register is not sufficient to establish all qualification rules.
evaluations.judge_ruling: Substantially matched, 4/5. The audit cycle is documented, while the detailed auditor qualification and follow-up method needs fuller support.
evaluations.rationale: Appendix B XVIII / NQA-1 Part I Requirements 18 and 2: retain 75 points using Manual 9.2, Prilog 2 and Dodatak 1 point 18. Completed audit files are a later verification sample, not a prerequisite for issuing this documentation score.

evaluations.affirmative_summary: Manual 5.3 and Prilog 2 §§1.2-1.3 assign duties, preserve responsibility after delegation, give QA personnel organizational freedom, and provide direct management access. PQ10.2-1 §2.9 gives management a stop-work duty on significant nonconformances.
evaluations.contrary_summary: The written organization rules do not clearly protect QA decisions when cost or schedule conflicts with nuclear safety. Management access and a stop-work route support independence, but do not fully settle that conflict.
evaluations.judge_ruling: Substantially matched, 4/5. The organization has defined authority and reporting routes; the safety-over-cost/schedule safeguard needs clarification under Appendix B I and NQA-1 Requirement 1 §201(d).
evaluations.rationale: Manual 5.3 and Prilog 2 give QA staff authority, freedom and direct reporting to management. The written rules do not clearly state how nuclear safety wins a cost or schedule conflict. This is a substantial match; test that safeguard in the real audit.

evaluations.affirmative_summary: Manual 7.1-7.3, 8.1 and 9.3 define resources, competence, work conditions, project quality plans and annual management review. Dodatak 1 §2 places NS/AQ work at level I. PQ7.1-1 §§2-3 requires planned training and competence records; PQ9.2 §3.8 defines nuclear auditor qualifications.
evaluations.contrary_summary: The program has a meaningful graded planning process. Its written nuclear inspection/test personnel qualification rules do not clearly set the periodic re-evaluation and inactivity checks in NQA-1 Requirement 2 §203. General training and certificate renewal do not fully define those checks.
evaluations.judge_ruling: Substantially matched, 4/5. The written program meets the main planning, resource, training and review duties. Nuclear inspection/test qualification maintenance needs clearer rules. An absent completed project plan is not treated as a missing generic planning process.
evaluations.rationale: Manual 8.1 requires quality plans with staff, methods, equipment, checks, acceptance criteria and records; Dodatak 1 §2 sets nuclear grading. Training and annual review are defined. Nuclear inspection/test qualification maintenance is less clear than NQA-1 Requirement 2 §203, so the program is a substantial match.

evaluations.affirmative_summary: Manual 8.3 and PQ8.3-1 §§3.1-3.5 control design inputs, interfaces, independent checks, release, records and changes. Software verification is triggered by configuration and use changes in Dodatak 1's flow notes.
evaluations.contrary_summary: The nuclear addendum and Prilog 5 use inconsistent RSP and ROS identifiers. The actual design-software verification method is not supplied, so the written chain to a proven calculation tool or independently verified result is incomplete.
evaluations.judge_ruling: Substantially matched, 4/5. The main design-control process is substantive. The software verification/reference chain needs clarification for NQA-1 Requirement 3 §§401 and 500. No blanket Part II compliance is assumed.
evaluations.rationale: Manual 8.3 and PQ8.3-1 define checked inputs, independent verification, controlled interfaces and changes. Conflicting RSP/ROS references leave the design-software verification route unclear. The written design process is a substantial match; verify the correct procedure and a calculation in the real audit.

evaluations.affirmative_summary: Manual 8.4 and PQ8.4-2 §3.2 require technical and QA requirements, acceptance methods, access rights, record controls, nonconformance reporting, lower-tier flow-down and document delivery times. Named staff prepare, review and approve the purchase documents; Manual 8.4.4 applies contract-document change controls.
evaluations.contrary_summary: No specific missing written procurement-document duty is identified in the reviewed scope. Real-audit sampling must confirm that nuclear purchase documents use the required clauses, including lower-tier flow-down and record/submittal terms.
evaluations.judge_ruling: Fully matched for documentation, 5/5. PQ8.4-2 §3.2 and Manual 8.4 cover the procurement-document intent of Appendix B IV and NQA-1 Requirement 4 §§200-400. This is not a finding that every issued order has been checked.
evaluations.rationale: PQ8.4-2 §3.2 expressly requires lower-tier flow-down, record controls, access rights and document delivery times, alongside technical, QA and acceptance requirements. Manual 8.4 governs review and changes. The written procurement-document process is fully matched; inspect issued orders in the real audit.

evaluations.affirmative_summary: Manual 3 defines qualified procedures and special processes; 8.5.2 commits to validation and supervision of such work. PQ7.5-4 §3.1 requires personnel/equipment qualifications and technical criteria in work procedures. Prilog 5 lists RVT, RPT, RMT and RUT methods.
evaluations.contrary_summary: The generic template and procedure titles do not establish the actual special-process qualification method. The supplied set does not show how a specific NDT method is demonstrated fit for purpose, how its parameters/acceptance limits are approved, and how current process, equipment and personnel qualifications are maintained.
evaluations.judge_ruling: Partially matched, 3/5. The policy and procedural framework are present, but method-specific qualification controls remain weakly evidenced against NQA-1 Requirement 9 §§201-203 and 400. Coatings, concrete, epoxy and non-metal testing are scope questions, not assumed Ekonerg activities.
evaluations.rationale: Manual 8.5.2 requires special-process validation and supervision, and Prilog 5 identifies NDT methods. The reviewed documents do not show a complete method-specific qualification and current-qualification control route. This is a partial match; request the relevant RVT/RPT/RMT/RUT methods and qualification rules in the real audit.

evaluations.affirmative_summary: Manual 7.5.1 and 8.5.1 require detailed work instructions with prerequisites, people, equipment, responsibilities, acceptance criteria and reporting. PQ7.5-4 §3.1 specifies those contents and §3.3 requires competent preparation, independent review and approval.
evaluations.contrary_summary: No specific missing general instruction-content duty is identified. Task-specific RVT/RPT/RMT/RUT and RSP/ROS methods still need real-audit checks in their own technical areas; a title alone is not proof that a special method is qualified.
evaluations.judge_ruling: Fully matched for documentation, 5/5. The written instruction framework covers Appendix B V and NQA-1 Requirement 5 §100, including acceptance criteria and detail suited to the task. This does not approve every listed technical method.
evaluations.rationale: Manual 7.5.1 and PQ7.5-4 §3.1 require clear work steps, qualified staff and equipment, acceptance criteria and required records. Review, approval and distribution are assigned. The written instruction framework is fully matched; technical method qualification remains a separate check under the relevant criterion.

evaluations.affirmative_summary: Manual 7.5.3 and PQ7.5-5 §§3-4 assign preparation, review, approval, changes and controlled distribution. They require current copies at use, revision status, controlled external documents and withdrawal or marking of obsolete copies.
evaluations.contrary_summary: The supplied manual has conflicting references: Dodatak 1 §11 cites ROS-02 for software control while Prilog 5 lists ROS-03; §17 cites RSP-03 for backup while the register lists ROS-04. These are live navigation ambiguities, not merely absent work samples.
evaluations.judge_ruling: Substantially matched, 4/5. Document-control duties are written and assigned. Conflicting controlled references prevent an unqualified full match under NQA-1 Requirement 6 §§100-300.
evaluations.rationale: Manual 7.5.3 and PQ7.5-5 define approval, revision, distribution and current copies at use. The manual's ROS-02/ROS-03 and RSP-03/ROS-04 references conflict with its procedure register. The process is a substantial match; resolve which controlled methods staff must use.

evaluations.affirmative_summary: Manual 8.4, PQ8.4-2 §§3.1-3.4 and PQ8.4-3 §§3.2-3.9 define supplier selection, nuclear qualification, graded surveillance, acceptance and performance review. Supplier evidence is checked against requirements and retained; Dodatak 1 §7 defines safety significance, critical characteristics and verification selection for commercial products.
evaluations.contrary_summary: Commercial-product dedication is described at a high level, without the detailed acceptance route. Manual 8.4.3 describes conformity evidence before/after installation, which does not clearly secure required evidence before installation or use for safety-related hardware.
evaluations.judge_ruling: Substantially matched, 4/5. The service procurement and supplier-control process is substantive. The safety-related hardware acceptance timing and detailed commercial-product route need confirmation under Appendix B VII and NQA-1 Requirement 7 §501. No blanket Part II obligation is added.
evaluations.rationale: Manual 8.4 and PQ8.4-2/PQ8.4-3 require supplier evaluation, nuclear qualification, checks and acceptance records. Safety-related hardware evidence timing and the detailed commercial-product acceptance route are less clear. The supplier-control process is a substantial match, not a review of other companies as separate audit targets.

evaluations.affirmative_summary: Manual 8.5.3 maintains project and study identity through work-order and document identifiers. Sections 8.5.4-8.5.5 control customer property and preservation. Dodatak 1 §8 requires a nuclear document defining traceability methods, special requirements and marking authority.
evaluations.contrary_summary: The process is clear for engineering deliverables. The generic nuclear hardware rules do not clearly cover identity transfer on subdivision, replacement of damaged storage marks, or limited-life item expiry under NQA-1 Requirement 8 §§202 and 302-303.
evaluations.judge_ruling: Substantially matched, 4/5. The stated engineering-service scope has a meaningful identity and traceability process. The remaining gap concerns the generic hardware safeguards, not the absence of a completed job-specific marking record.
evaluations.rationale: Manual 8.5.3 links engineering work to work-order and document identifiers; Dodatak 1 §8 requires nuclear marking and traceability planning. The service process is a substantial match. Written hardware safeguards for split items, damaged marks and shelf-life expiry need clarification where that work is undertaken.

evaluations.affirmative_summary: Manual 8.6 and 9.1.4 require documented checks, acceptance, witness/hold points and indirect monitoring when inspection is unsuitable. PQ8.6 §§3.2-3.7 assigns competent independent checking and record duties; repaired work is verified again.
evaluations.contrary_summary: The hold-point planning rule does not clearly require recorded consent before a hold point is waived, as NQA-1 Requirement 10 §300 requires. The real audit should also confirm exclusion of both the performer and direct supervisor from acceptance inspections.
evaluations.judge_ruling: Substantially matched, 4/5. Inspection planning, independence, records and reinspection are defined. The written hold-point waiver safeguard needs clarification; lack of a completed inspection report alone is not the reason for the rating.
evaluations.rationale: Manual 9.1.4 and PQ8.6 define planned independent checks, records, release and reinspection; witness and hold points are required. Prior recorded approval for waiving a hold point is not clearly prescribed. The inspection process is a substantial match.

evaluations.affirmative_summary: Manual 9.1.4 requires customer testing to have a program, written requirements, acceptance criteria, suitable conditions, records and result evaluation. Manual 7.5.1, PQ7.5-4 §3.1 and 7.1.5 provide prerequisites, qualified staff/equipment and calibration controls. Software verification is tied to defined change/use triggers.
evaluations.contrary_summary: The software-control procedure reference conflicts with Prilog 5, and the full verification method is not supplied. The nuclear test-record content is not clearly specified to the detail of NQA-1 Requirement 11 §601, including deviations and the person evaluating results.
evaluations.judge_ruling: Substantially matched, 4/5. The written customer-testing process has the core test-control duties. Software-method identification and test-record detail need clarification. The manual's no-own-product-testing statement is preserved and does not cancel customer-testing duties.
evaluations.rationale: Manual 9.1.4 defines customer test programs, acceptance criteria, conditions, records and result evaluation; shared instruction and equipment rules supply prerequisites. Software-method references and detailed nuclear test-record fields remain unclear. The written testing process is a substantial match.

evaluations.affirmative_summary: Manual 7.1.5 and PQ7.1-2 §§2-3 require equipment identification, periodic checks/calibration, assigned owners, status evidence and records. Overdue equipment is marked and removed from use; repeatedly faulty equipment is repaired or replaced. Commercial devices may be exempt only when they give the required precision.
evaluations.contrary_summary: The supplied procedure does not clearly require tracing equipment to its use and evaluating prior results back to the last acceptable calibration when equipment is lost, damaged or out of calibration. These are written-control gaps under NQA-1 Requirement 12 §§303.1-303.2.
evaluations.judge_ruling: Substantially matched, 4/5. Calibration, ownership, status and exclusion duties are substantive. Use traceability and the look-back check need clearer instructions. The qualified commercial-device exception is consistent in intent with Requirement 12 §304 and is not treated as a failure.
evaluations.rationale: Manual 7.1.5 and PQ7.1-2 define calibration intervals, responsible owners, records and removal of overdue equipment. The written rule for tracing use and checking earlier results after equipment failure is incomplete. Equipment control is a substantial match; confirm that look-back process in the real audit.

evaluations.affirmative_summary: Manual 8.5.5 requires controlled handling, storage, cleaning, packaging, preservation and shipment to prevent damage, loss and deterioration. Sensitive items are marked and their conditions checked; project plans define special protection and handler competence.
evaluations.contrary_summary: The general preservation process is substantive. For special handling tools, the supplied rule does not clearly prescribe inspection/testing before use or at defined intervals, as NQA-1 Requirement 13 §400 requires when such tools are needed.
evaluations.judge_ruling: Substantially matched, 4/5. Written preservation and special-condition controls cover the main duty. The special handling-tool check needs clarification only where that equipment is used; no unsupported claim about Ekonerg operating a warehouse or crane is made.
evaluations.rationale: Manual 8.5.5 controls handling, storage, cleaning, packaging and shipment, with special marking, condition checks and trained handlers. It does not clearly prescribe pre-use or periodic checks of special handling tools. The preservation process is a substantial match for the stated scope.

evaluations.affirmative_summary: Manual 8.6 and 9.1.4 require acceptance evidence and an authorized release before delivery; nonconforming release requires special approval. Calibration status is marked and overdue equipment excluded. Dodatak 1 §14 requires a nuclear status document with a method, traceability and marking authority.
evaluations.contrary_summary: The service-release process is clear. The generic nuclear status rule does not clearly prescribe who may remove status marks and how an unsafe operating status or bypass is prevented under NQA-1 Requirement 14 §100.
evaluations.judge_ruling: Substantially matched, 4/5. Written service acceptance and release controls are present, along with nuclear status planning. The remaining concern is the generic status-removal/operating safeguard, not a demand for completed plant tag records from an engineering-service supplier.
evaluations.rationale: Manual 8.6 and 9.1.4 require accepted work and authorized release, and Dodatak 1 §14 requires nuclear status planning. Authority to remove status marks and safeguards against operating-status bypass are not clear. The documented status-control process is a substantial match.

evaluations.affirmative_summary: Manual 8.7 and PQ10.2-1 §§2-3 define immediate reporting, marking/segregation or other safeguards, evaluation, approved disposition, prevention of use and verified completion. PQ8.3-1 §3.5 applies original design controls to changes caused by a nonconformance.
evaluations.contrary_summary: Use-as-is or repair decisions do not clearly require a documented technical justification and matching as-built records as specified by NQA-1 Requirement 15 §404. Customer consent and QA approval are meaningful, but do not by themselves supply that technical basis. Part 21 reporting remains a separate unresolved follow-up.
evaluations.judge_ruling: Substantially matched, 4/5. The written prevention, disposition and re-verification process is substantial. Technical justification and as-built treatment for repair/use-as-is need clarification. This rating covers Appendix B XV, not a finding of full Part 21 compliance.
evaluations.rationale: Manual 8.7 and PQ10.2-1 control reporting, segregation, disposition, approval and re-verification; design changes follow original design controls. A mandatory technical justification and matching as-built record for repair/use-as-is are not clear. Nonconformance control is a substantial match; Part 21 reporting is a separate follow-up.

evaluations.affirmative_summary: Manual 8.7, 9.2, 10.2 and Prilog 2 require prompt action, significant/repeated cause review, recurrence prevention, records, management reports and verified completion/effectiveness. PQ10.2-2 §§2.2, 2.5, 2.7 and 3.1-3.8 assign approval, follow-up, reopening and reporting duties.
evaluations.contrary_summary: No missing Appendix B XVI written corrective-action duty is identified. The real audit must sample timely and effective completion. Part 21 remains applicable: the reporting route beyond the customer notification described in PQ10.2-1 §3.11 remains unresolved, and is not included in XVI's Appendix B score.
evaluations.judge_ruling: Fully matched for documentation, 5/5. The written controls cover Appendix B XVI and NQA-1 Requirement 16 §100. Part 21 reporting is outside this criterion's score and remains unresolved; full here does not mean full Part 21 compliance or verified execution.
evaluations.rationale: Manual 8.7, 9.2 and 10.2 plus PQ10.2-2 require prompt correction, significant-condition cause analysis, recurrence prevention, records, management reporting and verified completion. The written corrective-action process is fully matched. Part 21 reporting remains applicable and unresolved, outside XVI's Appendix B score.

evaluations.affirmative_summary: Manual 7.5.4, PQ7.5-7 §§3.1-3.8 and Prilog B define record identity, review, responsibility, retention and lifetime nuclear records. Electronic media are checked/copied within five years; Dodatak 1 §17 describes a central archive, a server and a remote parallel server.
evaluations.contrary_summary: The backup method is cited as RSP-03 while Prilog 5 lists ROS-04. The supplied storage rules do not fully define protection/access and continued retrieval through hardware/software changes under NQA-1 Requirement 17 §§601 and 800. Five-year copying and remote storage are credited, not ignored.
evaluations.judge_ruling: Substantially matched, 4/5. Identification, retention, responsibility and physical/electronic preservation are substantive. The backup reference and long-term access/retrieval safeguards need clearer controlled instructions.
evaluations.rationale: PQ7.5-7 defines record identity, approval, retention, lifetime nuclear records and five-year media copying; the manual requires remote server copies. Conflicting backup references and incomplete access/technology-change retrieval rules leave a written gap. Record control is a substantial match.

evaluations.affirmative_summary: Manual 9.2 and PQ9.2 §§3.2-3.8 require planned and extra audits, independent trained auditors, checklists, reports to management, responses and verified follow-up. Nuclear lead-auditor qualification includes five audits in three years with a recent nuclear audit, continuing participation and an annual-evaluation form.
evaluations.contrary_summary: PQ8.4-3 §3.8 reviews supplier performance after engagements and PQ9.2 §3.2 prescribes triennial nuclear supplier audits. A required annual evaluation, or a formally reviewed ongoing alternative, between supplier audits is not clearly set out for all approved nuclear suppliers under NQA-1 Requirement 18 §202.
evaluations.judge_ruling: Substantially matched, 4/5. The audit process and nuclear auditor qualification duties are substantive. The supplier performance-review interval needs clarification. Completed audit records are real-audit samples, not a prerequisite for crediting this written process.
evaluations.rationale: Manual 9.2 and PQ9.2 define planned independent audits, qualified nuclear auditors, reports and verified follow-up. Supplier reviews occur after work and audits at least every three years. The annual or formally reviewed ongoing evaluation between nuclear supplier audits is not clear, so this is a substantial match.
